title: Zero data retention with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards is now in beta
summary: Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), a misuse-detection layer compatible with zero data retention, has moved from private beta with Bridgewater, Salesforce, and Stripe to public beta. It monitors misuse patterns across many requests and creates Safety Cases for customer review, while customers supply their own S3 or GCS storage and data is deleted after write and never used for training. It is available on Claude Platform, Platform on AWS, Bedrock, and Google Cloud, with Microsoft Foundry coming soon.

title: KPMG's Todd Lohr on AI when your data is also your clients' data
summary: In an interview, KPMG US Vice Chair Todd Lohr discusses deploying frontier AI with sensitive client data. KPMG integrated Claude into its Digital Gateway tax platform as "Digital Gateway Powered by Claude" and is an early user of Enterprise Frontier Safeguards to keep data within its own organization. Automated misuse review flags serious misuse for human review, and his advice is to "adopt and secure at the same time."

title: How the Claude Code team thinks about verification
summary: An engineering post by Addy Osmani explains how agents verify work with evidence, noting that Claude writes about 90% of the Claude Code team's code. It covers three test types (end-to-end, property, and differential), practices such as a per-repo verify skill, a 39-item reliability checklist, and REVIEW.md read from the base branch, and a commit gate with off, observe, and enforce modes. A separate grader improved task success by up to 10 points, shifting the human role toward defining "done."

title: Building strong safety evaluations
summary: Anthropic's engineering guide covers designing, running, and reporting AI safety evaluations. It recommends measuring appropriate response rate with domain rubrics rather than refusal rate, and using multi-turn simulations because single-turn tests saturate. It also stresses validating graders against experts, preregistering, repeating runs, and reporting confidence intervals, and notes that a targeted system prompt raised appropriate response rate from 60% (API) to 94% on claude.ai.

title: MCP servers can now ship skills, run tasks, and more with Claude
summary: MCP servers can now publish skills alongside tools, with Skills over MCP in public beta so skills load on demand and update with the server. Tasks (background long jobs) and Elicitation (pausing for user sign-off or input) are now generally available, and File Uploads for sending PDFs, spreadsheets, and images to servers is rolling out soon. Because this is part of the open spec, other compatible clients should be able to support it as well.

title: Turn artifacts into Mac and Windows apps
summary: Artifacts can be installed as desktop apps on Mac and Windows via "Install as app" (beta), each getting its own icon and window, sharing support, and auto-updating when the artifact is edited. Three permission levels are offered: a browser-like default, app permissions for notifications and shortcuts, and full computer access, which lets artifacts act as everyday work tools such as calendar-driven meeting prep with reminders. It is available on all plans but not for HIPAA-ready orgs or hybrid deployments, and it requires internet access and sign-in.
